methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria from EHR. Appropriate survival analysis including Kaplan-Meier curves and competing risk analyses for CSCC-specific death. Cox proportional hazards models used for prognostic factor evaluation. However, limited to single center (Dana-Farber), genomic data available in only 27.7% (20/72 patients), and small subgroups for mechanistic analysis (neoadjuvant n=7). Missing discussion of EHR data quality validation and no prespecified primary outcomes.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses clinically important and understudied problem of managing CSCC after anti-PD-1 therapy failure. Identifies prognostic factors (prior chemotherapy associated with poorer OS: HR 2.87, P=0.04) and characterizes subsequent treatment patterns (cetuximab, local therapy, anti-PD-1 rechallenge) with response rates. Median OS 44.1 months provides direct clinical guidance for treatment sequencing post-immunotherapy.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods section clearly describes cohort selection (238 patients screened, 72 with progression), outcome definitions (EFS1/EFS2 distinction), and statistical approaches (Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, competing risk). Missing elements: formal pre-specification of primary outcome, detailed competing risk methodology, power calculation, and explicit missing data handling. Patient flow diagram provided but supplementary data redacted. No statement of data availability or repository for future researchers.

novelty_literature.justification: Extends understanding of resistance mechanisms to anti-PD-1 in CSCC. TMB-resistance association is novel finding in this context (primary resistance TMB 23.19 vs secondary 71.51, P=0.03). However, predominant progression patterns (metastatic > locoregional) and treatment options (cetuximab, RT) align with established literature. Single-center retrospective analysis without multicenter validation limits impact.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with effective visual communication. Sankey diagram clearly shows metastatic site transitions, Kaplan-Meier curves effectively depict survival, and swimmer plot comprehensively documents clinical course. Table 1 thoroughly presents baseline and treatment characteristics. Some redundancy in Introduction (unmet need stated twice). Figures effectively communicate progression dynamics and treatment patterns.

key_strengths: Clinically important cohort: 72 CSCC patients with anti-PD-1 failure representing rare and understudied population
Appropriate survival methodology using competing risk analysis to account for CSCC-specific versus non-CSCC mortality
Novel finding: tumor mutational burden significantly lower in primary resistance (median 23.19) versus secondary resistance (71.51), P=0.03
Comprehensive treatment characterization documenting subsequent therapy outcomes including cetuximab response rate, local therapy efficacy, and anti-PD-1 rechallenge benefit
Incorporation of diverse treatment contexts including neoadjuvant, palliative, and adjuvant settings with documented outcomes
key_concerns: Limited genomic data: only 27.7% (20/72) underwent sequencing, reducing statistical power for TMB-resistance association analysis
Single-center retrospective design with Dana-Farber institutional bias and potential for unmeasured confounding variables
Small subgroups for mechanistic analysis: neoadjuvant arm only 7 patients, secondary resistance with sequencing only 6 patients
No multiple comparison adjustment in univariate filtering before multivariate Cox modeling, increasing type I error risk
Response assessment hindered by 36% non-assessable rate in subsequent treatment analysis due to patients receiving local therapy
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-executed retrospective cohort analysis with appropriate methods and novel prognostic insights. Clinical relevance and sound methodology warrant tier 3 placement, though single-center design and limited genomic data prevent higher tier consideration.
